name: Nekkar
description: A star 69 parsecs away, 19 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 73555: radius 18.673 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 198.63 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.051) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 73555: effective temperature 5018 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.077)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 2.8 from 2025A&A...698A..93J; the 17 published values span log g 2.35 to 3.06, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 73555: distance 69.061 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.01), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 69 parsecs away, 19 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 199 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,018 K, so 18.673 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 73555: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Boötis
quotes.card: Beta Boötis is a star in the northern constellation of Boötes.
quotes.introduction: Its name is a Bayer designation that is Latinised from β Boötis, and abbreviated Beta Boo or β Boo.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1296713990316692096 (quality A), from 2015A&A...574A..50J; Gaia DR3 measures none
